description: A pearl-gray haze of primordial particulate fills a sphere a third of an astronomical unit wide, glowing faintly at wavelengths that predate ordinary chemistry. Within it, matter refuses to settle: solids soften, gases thicken, and sampled material returns to the lab already decaying into unfamiliar isotopes. Sensors read baryon densities that should only have existed minutes after the Big Bang.

The Concordance contracts with tidal patience, drawing inward a few thousand kilometers per year and compressing whatever it holds into states no crucible can reach. Probes inserted at the boundary transmit for hours, then simply stop being matter. Readings inside suggest particles negotiating which laws to obey.

Cosmologists located the haze while hunting the universe's missing primordial inventory, and half of cosmology now hangs on what they find there. Its age is measured at 13.6 billion years, making it effectively a fossil of the first instants. Three Nobel-equivalents have been awarded for work conducted from its edge.

Access is rationed by an academic consortium that guards sampling windows like harvest seasons. The contraction shows no sign of stopping, and models disagree wildly about what the core becomes when the last of it closes. Whatever is gestating in there, everyone wants to watch it happen.
